about: How a commander's camera names are drawn, and where the Camera Commander card puts its Talk chips: each commander's `labels`. Each option: label, help, default, and its range or its choices (neither: a colour). `fonts`: the file of each font but the standard one (Pillow's built-in), in the casa_mia component's www/fonts. Read by the compositor (compositor/labels.py), the app's checks, the cards (integration/cards/src/labels.ts) and the admin page. Not in layout.json, which Sensor Watch's cards bundle.

font.label: Font
font.help: The font the cameras' names are in. Standard is the one they were always in; a live main camera's name is then in the browser's own font.

tile_size.label: Tile name size, px
tile_size.help: The height of a tile's name. A screen with more pixels draws it with more of them, so it looks the same size everywhere.

main_size.label: Main camera name size, px
main_size.help: The height of the main camera's name and of the clock beside it.

colour.label: Text colour
colour.help: The colour of the names and the clock.

opacity.label: Background opacity, %
opacity.help: How solid the colour behind a name is. 0 leaves the name alone on the picture.

tile_style.label: A tile's name
tile_style.help: Bar: across the foot of the tile. Pill: only as wide as the name. None: no name.

main_style.label: The main camera's name
main_style.help: Bar: across the foot of the main camera. Pill: only as wide as the name. None: no name; the clock stays.

talk_status.label: Call status at
talk_status.help: Where the call's state (ringing, answered, time left) goes over the main camera. Put it clear of the date and name your cameras write on their own picture.

talk_buttons.label: Talk buttons at
talk_buttons.help: Where the Talk and hold-to-talk buttons go over the main camera.
